missions.name: kip
missions.summary: kip turns the rotation of people raising a newborn into one team: parents, grandparents, nannies and night doulas share one log, every entry signed with a face, so no detail is lost between shifts.
missions.objective-cadet: Babies aren’t raised by one tired parent. They’re raised by a rotation: two parents, a grandparent, a nanny, a night doula. Baby trackers tend to assume one person holding the phone; kip is built for the rotation. Every feed, nap, diaper and dose lands in one shared log with the face of whoever logged it, a handoff card briefs the next person before they ask, roles give each person exactly what they need, and plain-sentence patterns go to the parents, never diagnoses. The ambition: nothing dropped between shifts, no dose given twice by accident, and checkups that start with real data instead of guesses. It’s a [[Test flight]], a concept with no app yet, so the site lets you try it as any of the five people in June’s day.
missions.objective-engineer: Eleven pages and a real 404, coded by hand after ideation and wireframes, with no framework. A GSAP-scrubbed ribbon follows one day through four handoffs, a Try it page runs the shared log in memory (switching people is a handoff, and vitamin D asks before a second dose), a role builder redraws each person's phone, and a pediatrician report rebuilds across three ranges and prints only the paper. Dark mode is one token swap, Command-K search covers every page, every page reads without JavaScript, and motion rests under [[Reduced motion]].
missions.params:
Tell caregivers apart by shape alone at 3am
Roles and permissions, not all-or-nothing sharing
Patterns, not diagnoses
Every demo runs in the browser, and nothing is sent anywhere
No invented users, reviews, ratings or app-store badges
missions.benefits:
Know who fed her last without texting anyone: every entry carries the face of whoever logged it
Start every shift caught up: a handoff card shows what happened since you last had the phone
No accidental double doses: kip shows who already gave vitamin D today and asks before logging another
Share only what each person needs: Nana logs feeds without seeing the med history, and alerts stay with the parents
missions.manifest-pages: Home, Try it, Village, Insights, App tour, Pricing, Privacy, Questions, Early access, What's new, About, 404
missions.manifest-collections: App screens: Today, Log a feed, Village, Invite, Insights, Export, Night mode, Handoff, Milestones
missions.handoff: A static site that uploads anywhere, five demos that run in the browser and send nothing, nine app screens on a design canvas and a character set ready for the real app.

missions.name: CKS
missions.client: Product site · for the Knowledge System add-on
missions.summary: The product site for the Complete Knowledge System: a Stripe-grade SaaS site where visitors watch the same components change clothes for any brand, publish an entry and see the site rebuild, and try the Voice Kit.
missions.objective-cadet: The Knowledge System case study shows how it works inside a client's site. This mission sells it: a product site that lets a founder see it match their brand, feel how easy an update is, and try the Voice Kit before booking an install.
missions.objective-engineer: Five hand-coded pages. A canvas loom hero that pauses offscreen, a token-driven style lab where five site personalities and a bring-your-own panel re-skin the same components live, a publish demo that rebuilds the library, topic page and JSON-LD, and an interactive Voice Kit with a real approval gate.
missions.params:
Show style matching, don't claim it
An update a non-developer understands in 10 seconds
Nothing publishes without approval, even in the demo
No promised rankings, citations or timelines
Only one outcome number, and it's real
missions.manifest-pages: Home, How it works, Styles, Voice Kit, Pricing
missions.manifest-collections: Five site personalities, Knowledge graph, Publish demo, Voice Kit pipeline
missions.handoff: A static product site that uploads anywhere, with every demo running on the same tokens a client's site would use.
